brief.name: Protection of energy
brief.objective: Send readers to HLR’s two protection bracelets, then to The Scorpio Crystal Set, in the first days of Scorpio season.
brief.audience: HLR’s email subscribers. No segment data is on file.
brief.guidance: Vocabulary: protection, energy, black tourmaline, Scorpio season. Tone: the voice contract as written, short lines, one accent word in a headline. No figures; meaning only as tradition or intention; the Scorpio ideas are small rituals, never effects; no popularity line.

angle.copy2: Protection as a boundary you keep: black tourmaline, long held as a stone of protection, worn as the reminder.
angle.tension: By the end of a full day, other people’s energy is on you.

angle.why: It names a moment the reader knows from her own week (the book’s coworker’s bad vibes, p30), keeps the stone to tradition and the piece to a reminder, and hands over to Scorpio season without changing the subject.

scorpio.head: Scorpio season is here
scorpio.body:
Scorpio season has long been read as a time for depth and turning inward, and a few small rituals make room for it:

An evening with no plans, a candle lit, your phone in another room.

One thing you are ready to let go of, written down, then closed in a notebook.

Black tourmaline kept close, on your wrist or your altar, as a reminder of what is yours to tend.

notes.text: Scene not ratified: R1 is the brief’s own angle (protection of energy); inside it Claude developed scene 1 (the end of a full day) as the recommendation. Scenes 2 and 3 stay live; pick again and only the copy below the angle changes.

The two bracelets sit in the M06 grid under the heading Wear one, or both. They were first built as M03 spotlights with the eyebrows WEAR ONE and OR BOTH, but at M03’s name size (the locked headline style in a 338 px column) Tourmaline and Protection broke inside the word; the grid sets the full names in the title style without a break. The Scorpio Crystal Set keeps M03, whose short words fit.

Eddie edited the build live on 2026-10-23 and his edits stand: he cut the text block's first sentence (By the end of a full day, other people’s energy can follow you home.), so the slate now carries his body; he switched on the hero’s script line, which still shows the placeholder (a script line) and needs his line or the option off before export; and he moved the frame.

Products resolved from products.json: the-classic-bracelet-in-black-tourmaline, the-seeds-of-protection-bracelet, the-scorpio-crystal-set. Descriptions are empty and the set lists no contents, so the copy states no metal, size, price or stone list; the one product fact used is the stone each bracelet carries (Black Tourmaline).
No popularity line: Eddie names the two bracelets HLR’s top two protection sellers, and no sales source is on file (HLR-T01). Donnie can add BEST SELLERS as an eyebrow once the source is.

The subject and preheader were drafted from the voice contract alone: the exemplar file has no subject or preheader lines. The pack has no favorites yet, so every gate saw historical exemplars only; no measured preference is on file, so the checklist carries the voice contract’s five checks and the brief items.

Type product_spotlight read live from type-registry-core.json (ratified). Product names in the spotlights are data-fed from products.json (M03.name) and listed in cuts only to prove they fit; the footer carries HLR-REQ-01 verbatim in M09 and is not redrafted here.
Every composed string fit its slot budget, so the cut pass changed nothing: cuts lists each mapped string unchanged so fit_check can confirm the budgets.
Each headline names its accent word (field accent); the build sets that word in the headline accent style.

The protection and stone lines are framed as tradition or intention (HLR-M01, HLR-M05) and the footer carries the disclaimer; the ledger is a test seed (hlr-ledger-0.2.0), so no line here is cleared for production until HLR names its claims signer (C2).

Library gap: M03.name breaks any word longer than about eight letters inside the word at the email headline size (338 px column); its flex probe proved length, not word width. Logged for the next library pass beside E07’s hand-setting flag.
